description: EXHAUSTIVE d=64 sweep (bf16, hstu) = full block-tile grid PLUS the base-tile kernels. The tile grid is over sequence<kM0,kN0,kN0Sub,kN1,kK1,MaxK>: M=km0 {64,128,192}, N=kn0 {32,64,128}, K-stream=kn0sub+kk1 (must be equal; sweep kk1 {32,64}, kn0sub auto-matched in the instance_gen gate), V head tile kn1 {16,32,64}, at the dispatch-default WarpK=16 (warp_k=0, 16x16x16 MFMA — the geometry the deployed example binary launches via try_run_tuned_jagged_forward /*WarpK=*/16 /*KN0=*/32, verified BIT-EXACT vs the maxk128 reference). warp_k=32 (16x16x32, the `_wk32` variant) is intentionally EXCLUDED from the tile family: although it compiles and is faster, it is numerically BROKEN (149 sign-flip mismatches vs the maxk128 reference), so keeping it in the grid would let a broken kernel be surfaced as BEST. The base-tile family is added by including 0 in every tile-dim axis (km0/kn0/kn0sub/kn1/kk1) with warp_k {0}: the instance_gen gates (tile dims all-or-nothing; warp_k=32=>tile; tile=>max_k=64) collapse the product to (a) the full tile grid at WarpK=16 and (b) base-tile kernels at the dispatch-default WarpK over max_k {64,96,128} x mtile {64,128} x splitkv {false,true} (split-KV needs mtile=64). The base-tile family includes the legacy heuristic kernel jagged_bf16_causal1_maxk64_mtile128_splitkv0, so the heur-vs-best row resolves EXACTLY (no '*' fallback). Invalid tile combos are skipped by instance_gen (kN0Sub==kK1, kN0%kK1==0, MaxK%kN1==0, kK1>=WarpK). splitkv with a tile override is skipped (split-KV dispatch cannot honor tile-shape overrides). Kernel names get _km0NNN _n0NNN _n0sNNN _n1NNN _k1NNN tokens when overridden. For finding the best tile shape per d=64 shape, not for quick iteration (use sweep_fast.json for that). Pass the shape inline, e.g. --batch 120 --num-head 4 --seqlen 16384 --hdim 64 --target-size 300.
